topics.title: Howard Stern Discusses GQ Recognition & Listener Reactions
topics.summary: During a broadcast, Howard Stern discusses his selection by Gentleman’s Quarterly magazine as a comedic voice. He clarifies the criteria – influence and notoriety – dismissing claims of being among the ‘funniest people in comedy,’ while callers express negative reactions including criticism from The Daily News and Sam Kennison's appearance.

topics.title: Radio Show Awards & Ethnic Concerns
topics.summary: During a radio show, panelists discuss an awards ceremony recognizing controversial media content like ‘Mississippi Burning’ and ‘License to Kill,’ criticizing stereotypes. Bill Forgays expresses concern over negative portrayals of various ethnic groups in entertainment – particularly Hispanic drug lords and Italian-American characters - arguing for greater sensitivity while dismissing concerns about offensive humor.

topics.title: Phone Calls, Hollywood Gossip & Unresolved Conflicts
topics.summary: During a chaotic phone call segment, hosts discuss past friendships with Bob Hope and Lee Iacocca while grappling with accusations of insensitive remarks. They debate racial slurs, criticize Sam Kennison’s behavior, and express confusion over Jessica Hahn's involvement in Hollywood drama, ultimately devolving into personal anecdotes about concert ticket sales and Bruce Willis sightings.

topics.title: Stern Awards and Celebrity Criticism
topics.summary: Radio host Howard Stern discusses the newly established ‘Golden Pit Award’ given out by a group including Bill Fageezi, known for his limousine business. The conversation shifts to criticisms of figures like Bob Hope and Lee Iacocca over their views on homosexuality and car seatbelts, culminating in an announcement of new awards with names such as 'Twisted Sphincter'.

topics.title: Awards and Insults
topics.summary: Howard Stern attempts to announce William D. Fagasi’s bizarre awards, involving conversations about Paul Shafer's dating life and a chaotic interview with the New York City Gay Men's Chorus. The broadcast devolves into insults directed at Barbara Walters and Leona Helmsley.

topics.title: Elvis Week - Unscripted Conversation
topics.summary: During an impromptu session honoring Elvis Presley’s death, the hosts engage in a bizarre conversation filled with technical difficulties – specifically concerning an echo chamber setup – interspersed with outlandish anecdotes about Janet Culver's habits (including urine consumption) and nonsensical song ideas. The discussion drifts into unrelated topics like Priscilla Presley, Nicholas Abbott, and various substances consumed by Elvis.
